subject: Regular expressions: words with a,e,i,o, and u

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Regular expressions: words with a,e,i,o, and u
parts:
Hi all

I have a two small regular expression questions. I have a character
vector v whose elements are individual words such as in the following:

rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))
v<-c("api", "documentation", "from", "the", "code", "result", "of",
"their", "evaluation", "is", "moskauerin")

Issue 1: I would like to retrieve all and only all words that contain
each of the five 'vowel characters' (i.e., "a", "e", "i", "o", "u"])
at least once. I think I have a solution but I am wondering whether
there is better one. My solution involves positive lookahead:

(matches<-grep("(?=\\w*a\\w*)(?=\\w*e\\w*)(?=\\w*i\\w*)(?=\\w*o\\w*)(?=
\\w*u\\w*)\\w+", v, perl=T, value=T)) # documentation, evaluation,
moskauerin

Question 1 is whether someone has a shorter / more elegant approach.

Issue 2: I would like to retrieve all and only all words that contain
each of the five 'vowel characters' (i.e., "a", "e", "i", "o", "u"])
exactly once. I have two solutions to this approach so far. One is to
apply the following line to the vector matches from above.

(matches.2a<-grep("\\b(?!\\w*?([aeiou])\\w*?\\1)\\w+", matches,
perl=T, value=T)) # moskauerin

The other is to apply one of the following two lines to v:

(matches.2b<-grep("\\b(?=\\w*a\\w*)(?=\\w*e\\w*)(?=\\w*i\\w*)(?=\\w*o\
\w*)(?=\\w*u\\w*)(?!\\w*?a\\w*?a)(?!\\w*?e\\w*?e)(?!\\w*?i\\w*?i)(?!\
\w*?o\\w*?o)(?!\\w*?u\\w*?u)\\w+", v, perl=T, value=T)) # moskauerin
(matches.2c<-grep("\\b(?=\\w*a\\w*)(?=\\w*e\\w*)(?=\\w*i\\w*)(?=\\w*o\
\w*)(?=\\w*u\\w*)(?!\\w*?([aeiou])\\w*?\\1)\\w+", v, perl=T, value=T))
# moskauerin

Question 2 is again whether someone has a shorter / more elegant
approach.

Any pointers would be greatly appreciated ...

Thanks,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Regular expressions: words with a,e,i,o, and u
parts:
I think these are clear cases where converting to sets or presorting
are simpler than regular expressions. Perhaps you can do these things
in R, else use Python with R (e.g. http://rpy.sourceforge.net/) and
use each for what it does best.

bafang:/tmp sb$ python
Python 2.5 (r25:51918, Sep 19 2006, 08:49:13)
>>> words = ["sequoia", "abacadabra", "yiieeaouuu!"]
>>> vowels = "aeiou"
>>> [w for w in words if set(w).issuperset(vowels)]
['sequoia', 'yiieeaouuu!']
>>> [w for w in words if sorted(c for c in w if c in vowels) == list(vowels)]
['sequoia']
>>>

-Steven Bird
